question.text: For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by \[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_D \Bigg( \bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}} \dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} + \bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}} \dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \Bigg) \: \textrm{d}A. \] From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
question.explanation:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

\[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S = \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A. \] Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

\[ \mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle. \]

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_x & = \left\langle 1, \: 0, \: \dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} \right\rangle \\[10pt] \mathbf{r}'_y & = \left\langle 0, \: 1, \: \dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} \right\rangle \end{align*}

Now, the fundamental vector product is

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_x \times \mathbf{r}'_y &= \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & 0 & \dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} \\ 0 & 1 & \dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} \end{vmatrix} = \left \langle -\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x}, \: -\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y}, \: 1 \right \rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} &= \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(x,y)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_x \times \mathbf{r}'_y) \,\textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D \langle P, \: Q, \: R \rangle \cdot \left \langle -\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x}, \: -\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y}, \: 1 \right \rangle \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D \Bigg( \bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\color{blue}-P} \dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} + \big(\bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\color{blue}-Q}\,\big) \dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \Bigg) \: \textrm{d}A. \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle x+y, \: 2x-y, \: x+z \right\rangle$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=2x-2y$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2$ and $-1 \leq y \leq 2.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ can be expressed as \[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \int_{0}^{2} \int_{-1}^{2} \fbox{$\phantom{AAAAAAA}$} \: \text{d}v \: \text{d}u. \] What is the missing expression?
question.explanation:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

\[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S = \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A. \]

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

\[ \mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: 2u-2v \right\rangle \]

over the domain

\[ D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 2, \: -1 \leq v \leq 2 \big\}. \]

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_u & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial x}{\partial u}, \: \dfrac{\partial y}{\partial u}, \: \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial u} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(u), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(v), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(2u-2v) \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 1, \: 0, \: 2 \right\rangle \\[10pt] \mathbf{r}'_v & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial x}{\partial v}, \: \dfrac{\partial y}{\partial v}, \: \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial v} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(u), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(v), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(2u-2v) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 0, \: 1, \: -2 \right\rangle \end{align*}

Now, the fundamental vector product is

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v &= \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & 0 &2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] & = \left \langle \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}, \: -\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 \end{vmatrix}, \: \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left \langle -2, \: 2, \: 1 \right \rangle. \end{align*}

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

\begin{align*} \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) &= \left\langle x+y, \: 2x-y, \: x+z \right\rangle \Big|_{x=u,\, \\ y=v,\, \\ z=2u-2v} \\[5pt] &= \left\langle u+v, \: 2u-v, \: u+(2u-2v) \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle u+v, \: 2u-v, \: 3u-2v \right\rangle \end{align*}

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) &= \left\langle u+v, \: 2u-v, \: 3u-2v \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle -2, \: 2, \: 1 \right\rangle \\[3pt] &=(u+v) \cdot (-2) + (2u-v) \cdot (2) + (3u-2v) \cdot 1 \\[3pt] &= -2u -2 v + 4u -2v+ 3u-2v \\[3pt] &= 5u-6v. \end{align}

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_S \left\langle x+y, \: 2x-y, \: x+z \right\rangle \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} &= \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D (5u-6v) \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2} \int_{-1}^{2} ( {\color{blue}5u-6v}) \: \textrm{d}v \: \textrm{d}u. \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle x^2-y^2, \: y^2-z^2, \: z^2 \right\rangle$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=-x-y$ for $-2 \leq x \leq 2$ and $-2 \leq y \leq 2.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ can be expressed as \[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \int_{-2}^{2} \int_{-2}^{2} \fbox{$\phantom{AAAAAAA}$} \: \text{d}v \: \text{d}u. \] What is the missing expression?
question.explanation:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

\[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S = \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A. \]

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

\[ \mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: -u-v \right\rangle \]

over the domain

\[ D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: -2\leq u \leq 2, \: -2 \leq v \leq 2 \big\}. \]

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_u & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial x}{\partial u}, \: \dfrac{\partial y}{\partial u}, \: \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial u} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(u), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(v), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(-u-v) \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 1, \: 0, \: -1 \right\rangle \\[10pt] \mathbf{r}'_v & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial x}{\partial v}, \: \dfrac{\partial y}{\partial v}, \: \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial v} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(u), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(v), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(-u-v) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 0, \: 1, \: -1 \right\rangle \end{align*}

Now, the fundamental vector product is

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v &= \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & 0 &-1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] & = \left \langle \begin{vmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix}, \: -\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 \end{vmatrix}, \: \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left \langle 1, \: 1, \: 1 \right \rangle. \end{align*}

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

\begin{align*} \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) &= \left\langle x^2- y^2, \: y^2-z^2, \: z^2 \right\rangle \Big|_{x=u,\, \\ y=v,\, \\ z=-u-v} \\[5pt] &= \left\langle u^2-v^2, \: v^2- (-u-v)^2, \: (-u-v)^2 \right\rangle \end{align*}

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) &= \left\langle u^2-v^2, \: v^2- (-u-v)^2, \: (-u-v)^2 \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle 1, \: 1, \: 1 \right\rangle \\[3pt] &= (u^2-v^2) \cdot (1) + (v^2- (-u-v)^2 )\cdot (1) + (-u-v)^2 \cdot 1 \\[3pt] &= u^2 - v^2 +v^2- (-u-v)^2+(-u-v)^2 \\[3pt] &= u^2 . \end{align}

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_S \left\langle x^2-y^2, \: y^2-z^2, \: z^2 \right\rangle \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} &= \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D u^2 \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \int_{-2}^{2} \int_{-2}^{2} {\color{blue}u^2 } \: \textrm{d}v \: \textrm{d}u. \end{align*}

question.text: For a surface $S$ given by $z = x^2y$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by \[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_D \Bigg( \bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\, xy + \bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,x^2 +R \Bigg) \: \textrm{d}A. \] From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
question.explanation:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

\[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S = \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A. \] Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=x^2y,$ it can be parameterized as

\[ \mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: x^2y \right\rangle. \]

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_x & = \left\langle 1, \: 0, \: 2xy \right\rangle \\[10pt] \mathbf{r}'_y & = \left\langle 0, \: 1, \: x^2 \right\rangle \end{align*}

Now, the fundamental vector product is

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_x \times \mathbf{r}'_y &= \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & 0 & 2xy \\ 0 & 1 & x^2 \end{vmatrix} = \left \langle -2xy, \: -x^2, \: 1 \right \rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} &= \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(x,y)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_x \times \mathbf{r}'_y) \,\textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D \langle P, \: Q, \: R \rangle \cdot \left \langle -2xy, \: -x^2, \: 1 \right \rangle \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D \Bigg( \bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\color{blue}-2P}\, xy + \left(\,\bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\color{blue}-Q}\,\right)\,x^2+R \Bigg) \: \textrm{d}A. \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle 2x-z, \: y-z, \: z+y\right\rangle$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=4x-y$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2$ and $-1 \leq y \leq 2.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ can be expressed as \[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \int_{0}^{2} \int_{-1}^{2} \fbox{$\phantom{AAAAAAA}$} \: \text{d}v \: \text{d}u. \] What is the missing expression?
question.explanation:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

\[ \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S = \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A. \]

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

\[ \mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: 4u-v \right\rangle \]

over the domain

\[ D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 2, \: -1 \leq v \leq 2 \big\}. \]

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_u & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial x}{\partial u}, \: \dfrac{\partial y}{\partial u}, \: \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial u} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(u), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(v), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}(4u-v) \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 1, \: 0, \: 4 \right\rangle \\[10pt] \mathbf{r}'_v & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial x}{\partial v}, \: \dfrac{\partial y}{\partial v}, \: \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial v} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(u), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(v), \: \dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}(4u-v) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 0, \: 1, \: -1 \right\rangle \end{align*}

Now, the fundamental vector product is

\begin{align*} \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v &= \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & 0 &4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] & = \left \langle \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix}, \: -\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 \end{vmatrix}, \: \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left \langle -4, \: 1, \: 1 \right \rangle. \end{align*}

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

\begin{align*} \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) &= \left\langle 2x-z, \: y-z, \: z+y \right\rangle \Big|_{x=u,\, \\ y=v,\, \\ z=4u-v} \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 2u-(4u-v), \: v-(4u-v), \: 4u-v+v \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle -2u+v, \: -4u+2v, \: 4u \right\rangle \end{align*}

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) &= \left\langle-2u+v, \: -4u+2v, \: 4u \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle -4, \: 1, \: 1 \right\rangle \\[3pt] &=(-2u+v) \cdot (-4) + (-4u+2v) \cdot 1 + 4u \cdot 1 \\[3pt] &= 8u - 4v + -4u+2v + 4u \\[3pt] &= 8u-2v. \end{align}

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_S \left\langle 2x-z, \: y-z, \: z+y \right\rangle \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} &= \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D ( 8u-2v) \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2} \int_{-1}^{2} {\color{blue} (8u-2v)} \: \textrm{d}v \: \textrm{d}u. \end{align*}
